Transport model

Source: R/transport_model.R
transport_model.Rd

This function converts a public transport data set in GTFS format into road segments between consecutive stops of each trip, with their times, distances and speeds, using the gtfs2gps package. The function also allows users to set the spatial resolution of the output and to keep the speed of public transport vehicles within a min_speed and max_speed range.

Usage

transport_model(
  gtfs_data,
  min_speed = 2,
  max_speed = 80,
  new_speed = NULL,
  parallel = NULL,
  ncores = 2,
  spatial_resolution = 100,
  output_path = NULL,
  continue = NULL
)

Arguments

gtfs_data

A path to a GTFS file or a GTFS data organized as a list of data.tables created with gtfstools::read_gtfs().

min_speed

numeric (in km/h) or a speed units value. Minimum valid speed, at least 2 km/h. Defaults to 2 km/h. Stop times are first adjusted with gtfstools::set_min_speed(), which can change the arrival and departure times of vehicles at transit stops. Segment speeds that are still below min_speed are then set to min_speed. The segment's duration becomes its distance divided by the new speed, and the later times of the trip are shifted by the difference (each trip keeps its first departure). Durations are rounded to whole seconds, so a very short segment (under about 11 m at 80 km/h) can keep 0 s.

max_speed

numeric (in km/h) or a speed units value. Maximum valid speed, at least 3 km/h. Defaults to 80 km/h. As for min_speed, stop times are first adjusted with gtfstools::set_max_speed(), and segment speeds still above max_speed are set to max_speed, with the trip's times shifted in the same way.

new_speed

numeric (in km/h) or a speed units value, between min_speed and max_speed. Speed used for segments without a speed; the trip's times are shifted as for min_speed. When new_speed = NULL (the default), the function uses the average speed (total distance / total time) of the trips of the same shape_id, after capping, or of the whole feed if the shape has none.

parallel

Deprecated. This argument is ignored, and using it gives a warning. Use ncores instead.

ncores

Number of threads used. Defaults to 2. If Inf, it uses all threads available, as given by data.table::getDTthreads(). Values above that number are reduced to it.

spatial_resolution

The spatial resolution in meters. Defaults to 100. The function only creates points in order to guarantee that the maximum distance between two consecutive points will be at most the spatial_resolution value. If a given GTFS shape_id has two consecutive points with a distance smaller than the spatial resolution, the algorithm will not remove such points.

output_path

character. A directory path. If NULL (default), the output is returned. Otherwise, the output of each shape_id is saved in this directory as an .rds file named after its shape_id, and nothing is returned. Characters that can't be in a file name on some systems (such as /, : or *) and % are written as %XX, their hexadecimal code, so utils::URLdecode() gives the id back (e.g. "a/b" is saved as a%2Fb.rds). The whole feed is still processed in memory. emission_model() reads every .rds file in this directory, so it should not contain files from other runs.

continue

Deprecated. This argument is ignored, and using it gives a warning. The whole feed is processed at once.

Value

An sf object (class c("sf", "data.frame"), CRS 4326) with one LINESTRING per segment between consecutive stops, from the first to the last stop of each trip, or NULL when output_path is provided (the outputs are then saved as files in output_path). Its columns are:

  • shape_id, trip_id, route_type, trip_number: the trip. For trips in frequencies.txt, trip_id gets a suffix for each departure (e.g. "1054020_1", "1054020_2");

  • from_stop_id, to_stop_id, stop_sequence: the segment's stops;

  • from_timestamp, to_timestamp (class ITime), and timestamp, equal to from_timestamp;

  • dist (km) and speed (km/h) of the segment, and cumdist (m) and cumtime (s), cumulative along the trip, all as units objects;

  • geometry.

See also

Other Core function: emission_model()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("gtfstools", quietly=TRUE)) {

# read GTFS
gtfs_file <- system.file("extdata/bra_cur_gtfs.zip", package = "gtfs2emis")
gtfs <- gtfstools::read_gtfs(gtfs_file)

# keep a single trip_id to speed up this example
gtfs_small <- gtfstools::filter_by_trip_id(gtfs, trip_id ="4451136")

# run transport model
tp_model <- transport_model(
  gtfs_data = gtfs_small,
  min_speed = 2,
  max_speed = 80,
  new_speed = 20,
  spatial_resolution = 100,
  ncores = 2)

head(tp_model)

  }
